newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica golden share won't hurt sale.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica golden share won't hurt sale.

text.p: The "golden share" that the government will retain in telecommunications group Telefonica after its privatisation will not reduce the issue's attractiveness, Telefonica Investment Relations director Francisco Blanco said on Monday.

"In any case the golden share won't reduce the attractiveness of the share at the upcoming privatisation and won't influence the future management of the company," Blanco said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
The Spanish government, which will sell its remaining 21 percent stake in Telefonica on the stock market early next year, said on Friday it would retain a golden share.

The golden share will allow the government special voting rights over a ten-year period. It maintains authorisation rights on items of strategic importance, such as liquidation, mergers and stake purhases of more than 10 percent.
